#### 1. Leber congenital amaurosis 11  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.391)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9679191)

**Proposed mechanism:** SIGMAR1 (HGNC:10642) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response and Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0034015|GO:0005886); Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response and Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0034015|GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ Motor Neuron Degeneration (HP:0003690); Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response and Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0034015|GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ Photoreceptor dysfunction (HP:0011700); Photoreceptor dysfunction (HP:0011700) —LEADS_TO→ Severe visual impairment (HP:0000598). Loss-of-function mutations in SIGMAR1 disrupt its role in ER stress response and calcium homeostasis. This disruption leads to motor neuron degeneration in AR-DSMA2 and photoreceptor dysfunction, ultimately causing severe visual impairment in LCA11.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SIGMAR1 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease, or if a distinct non-overlapping pathway is shown to be the primary driver of disease pathology in one of the conditions. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant in SIGMAR1 with a frequency >0.1% in gnomAD populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting SIGMAR1 function or downstream pathways involved in ER stress and calcium homeostasis could offer therapeutic strategies for both AR-DSMA2 and LCA11, suggesting a potential for shared treatment approaches.

#### 2. hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 5, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.388)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9679191)

Loss-of-function mutations in SIGMAR1 lead to disruption of the ER stress response, ultimately causing motor neuron degeneration. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in IL6R impair the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, resulting in compromised immune function and recurrent infections. While acting through distinct primary genes and pathways, both disruptions contribute to cellular dysfunction that can manifest as severe disease phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a common upstream regulatory mechanism or a shared downstream effector pathway that directly links SIGMAR1 dysfunction to IL6R function or vice versa, beyond their individual roles in cellular homeostasis and signaling, would falsify the proposed independent mechanistic chains converging on broad cellular dysfunction. _(variant: Identical loss-of-function variants in SIGMAR1 and IL6R found at high frequency (>1%) in the general population would suggest these are benign polymorphisms rather than disease-causing mutations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the independent yet convergent cellular disruptions caused by SIGMAR1 and IL6R mutations could inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, therapies targeting ER stress could potentially benefit patients with distal SMA 2, while immunomodulatory agents might be relevant for hyper-IgE syndrome. Identifying common downstream pathways, if any, could reveal novel therapeutic targets applicable to both conditions.
